newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 13.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Wednesday:
- Civil rights leaders called for a national boycott of Texaco Inc to protest against alleged racial problems inside the company.
- Interval Research Corp plans to spin off three of its entities.
- The management team at USAir Group Inc has proposed a new name, logo and paint job for the airline.
- Sunbeam Corp will cut its workforce by half in a major restructuring.
- The United States plans to promote China's quick entry into the World Trade Organization.
- French insurance giant AXA will buy rival UAP in a stock swap worth $9.02 billion.
- Controlling shareholder Ronald Perelman has offered to infuse Marvel Entertainment Group Inc with $350 million.
- The yield on the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond fell to its lowest level in eight months.
- Edouard Stern might not become the heir of investment bank Lazard Freres after an argument with his step father.
- Robert Stansky has overhauled Fidelity Magellan Fund during his first five months at the helm.
- A federal grand jury has handed the first indictments against stock promoters who were arrested in a sting operation in New York.
- Few U.S. athletes who won gold medals at the Atlanta Olympic games have signed endorsement contracts with major corporations.
